text:
julia-cs: Customer reporting JSON parse errors when using streaming=json mode. They say responses arrive but final object brace is missing, client throws "Unexpected end of JSON input". Request id 7f3a2c2c.

customer-acct: repro attached. Using our node client with fetch and reading stream. Sometimes last chunk seems to be empty. Happens ~1/200 requests. No downstream errors on our end; just parse failures.

marta-eng: thanks. can you paste the exact curl that reproduces it? also which edge region and are you going through any proxies/load balancers?

customer-acct: here's minimal curl we used from their environment: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"x-large","stream":true,"mode":"json","prompt":"{\\"q\\":\\"hi\\"}'}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?request_id=7f3a2c2c\\n```

customer-acct: After ~1s of tokens they get multiple SSE chunks, final chunk often just ends without final `}`.

sam-eng: can you confirm any middleboxes? Cloudflare, nginx, or internal proxy? Also what's the Content-Length behavior (should be chunked/transfer-encoding).

customer-acct: they said Cloudflare + an internal sidecar that injects keepalives. We saw `Connection: keep-alive` headers.

ingress-proxy-bot: proxy logs for request 7f3a2c2c: 
```
[2025-06-14T13:21:02Z] conn=3 request=7f3a2c2c upstream=api-pool-4 status=200 bytes_sent=4823 keepalive_probe=1
[2025-06-14T13:21:03Z] conn=3 request=7f3a2c2c upstream=api-pool-4 status=200 bytes_sent=4896 fin_sent=1
```

marta-eng: ingress log shows a FIN shortly after bytes_sent increased. That might be the client/proxy sending FIN after keepalive probe. Could lead to final chunk being dropped if runtime is mid-write. We need runtime logs for that request id. sam, can you follow up with runtime?

sam-eng: assigning to eng-runtime, starting trace collection. In the meantime, can you try forcing `--http1.1` or disabling intermediate keepalives? If it's reproducible with curl -N on public internet we can iterate quicker.

julia-cs: customer tried forcing http/1.1, still saw it but rate dropped. They also noted that if they add a small delay on client close (sleep 100ms) after stream end, their parser succeeds more often.

marta-eng: that suggests last TCP FIN might be racing with final chunk flush. I'll pull runtime write-path code and check that SSE framing flushes final `\n\n` and closes stream atomically. Could be our napi binding not flushing after last write when socket half-closed.

sam-eng: can someone capture a raw tcpdump of a failing session (pcap) and include hex of last few chunks? that'll prove whether server sends the final brace.

customer-acct: attaching pcap to ticket. also adding a minimal node repro using fetch readable stream: 
```js
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}` } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
let acc = '';
while(true){
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  acc += new TextDecoder().decode(value);
}
JSON.parse(acc); // sometimes throws
```

marta-eng: good repro. ops-oncall, marking this P2 for now but escalating if frequency increases. I'll add a defensive server-side final flush (sync write + socket cork uncork) as a mitigation and post a patch.

ops-oncall: acknowledged. if turnover to P1, page the oncall rotation.

sam-eng: created runtime ticket RUNTIME-4821, attaching pcap and proxy logs. next steps: (1) reproduce locally with same proxy keepalive behavior; (2) instrument final write path to confirm final bytes are sent; (3) ship hotfix to force flush and then verify with customer.

julia-cs: customer asked for ETA. please advise quick tests we can ask them to run that don't require code change.

marta-eng: ask them to set `Accept: text/event-stream` and add `--no-buffer` to curl, or run `curl --http1.1 -N` and keep the connection open for +200ms after stream end before closing client process. That will confirm race.

customer-acct: will run tests and report. thanks all.

marta-eng: noted. I'll follow up in RUNTIME-4821 with findings.
